rv.q: Her voice comes across here, fresh, strong and proud, in this reborn gem of a theatre in Hackney.
The Yard is the most significant new fringe venue in the capital of the past 20 years.
Violent, visceral and stylish, For Colored Girls is still a necessary piece of theatre.
It could hang a little longer in each section; before we have time to fully absorb its effects, we're already whizzing on to the next.
Page’s production sometimes feels rushed and lacking in clarity.
Despite the piece’s age, it still has the rawness and edginess of something created this year, and its insistence on the vitality of Black women’s lives has not lost its potency.
While the show does not always capture the full revolutionary spark, it’s still a moving revival of a groundbreaking piece of theatre.
This magnetic adaptation from Page and The Yard Theatre gives audiences a fantastic opportunity to see the theatrical trailblazer in all its glory.

Page’s production has an excellent cast, who deliver the necessary intensity and occasional hilarity, and perform choreographer Ingrid Mackinnon’s moves with evident pleasure as well as concentration.

A curious mix of over-reliance on the text itself and an unwillingness to completely pare down the presentation to allow it to come to the forefront means that a thrilling opening and conclusion are often let down by what comes between...
This is a production that could have been epic and legacy defining, but unfortunately feels a bit of a damp squib.

cn.t: Critics find this 50th-anniversary revival of Shange's groundbreaking choreopoem powerful and relevant, praising its unflinching exploration of Black womanhood through poetry and movement, though some feel the production doesn't fully realize its epic potential.
